newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian leu surge might hit exporters-traders.
newsitem.headline: Romanian leu surge might hit exporters-traders.

text.p: Romanian foreign exchange traders said on Thursday an upsurge in the local leu currency this week might hurt exporters if the trend continues and the central bank refrains from buying excess dollar liquidity.
"Exporters were extremely disappointed when I quoted them 6,800 lei to the dollar," said a trader with a state-run bank.
On Thursday, the leu soared to 6,700/7,000 to the dollar from its closing of 7,000/120 on Wednesday, reversing its gradual downtrend recorded earlier this month.

Traders said the firming of the leu followed the central bank's (BNR) move to halt dollar purchases since last Friday. They expected the leu to strenghten to around 6,500/6,900 by next week provided the BNR stays away from the market.
Central bank officials told Reuters they had been "closely monitoring" the market but declined to comment.

"In order to regulate the liquidity and financial flows on the market, the exchange and interest rates, the central bank is choosing the most flexible and optimal tools as well as specific central bank techniques," a BNR senior official said.
"Probably the BNR wants to avoid further leu liquidity injections and to sterilise part of leu funds it put on the market through its recent dollar purchases," said one trader.
But operators said a firmer leu could generate a short-term reluctancy among foreigners to invest in Romanian equities.
"A stronger leu will make stocks more expensive for foreign investors," said one trader with a foreign bank in Bucharest.
"Under the present market conditions I think the BNR should restart dollar purchases," another trader said.

Hard currency supply had constantly outrunned demand on the interbank market in recent months as foreign inflows rose due to growing interest in local equities, while dollar demand remained low with importers on the sidelines.
Such market features prompted the BNR to soak up dollars over the past months, imposing the leu's gradual slide.

The leu slipped to 7,280/330 to the dollar earlier this month after staying stable at about 7,050 in May, following a recovery from all-time lows of 9,000 in mid-February, when the BNR tightened monetary policies to combat rising inflation.
Its moves to mop up dollars have flooded the market with leu funds and triggered a rapid fall in money market rates to about 50 percent, from around 190 percent in early April.
That drop, combined with a fall in inflation to 4.3 percent last month from a record 30.7 percent in March, sent deposit rates down to 60 percent from about 100 percent previously.

Traders suggested the BNR's lack of action aimed to prevent a loss of confidence in the leu, having in mind the moves in interest rates and the leu's rates at the licensed money changing bureaux, where it dipped to about 7,400/700 last week from 7,170/300 and before firming to 7,200/500 this week.
